skill.name: codebase-design
skill.description: Shared vocabulary and process for designing deep modules with small interfaces, clean seams, testable adapters, and clearer refactoring trade-offs.
skill.summary: Design deeper modules by improving interfaces, seam placement, dependency injection, and tests.
skill.author: mattpocock

content.value_statement: Shallow module interfaces make code harder to change, test, and explain. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code a shared vocabulary for deeper module design.
actual_capabilities: Defines shared terms for modules, interfaces, seams, adapters, depth, leverage, and locality.
Guides reviews of module interfaces and identifies shallow pass-through designs.
Classifies dependencies so refactoring plans use suitable seams and adapters.
Recommends testing through the module interface instead of internal implementation details.
Provides a process for comparing several alternative interface designs.
limitations: Does not inspect code automatically without the user providing relevant files or context.
Does not generate production-ready architecture by itself.
Depends on project-specific constraints to make accurate design recommendations.
May need another domain skill for business vocabulary and product rules.

use_cases.title: Review a Module Interface
use_cases.description: Evaluate whether a module hides enough behavior behind a small, clear interface.

use_cases.title: Plan a Refactor
use_cases.description: Find shallow clusters and decide where a deeper module seam should live.

use_cases.title: Improve Test Strategy
use_cases.description: Move tests toward observable behavior through interfaces and away from implementation details.

prompt_templates.title: Review This Interface
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this module interface using the codebase-design vocabulary. Identify its interface, implementation, seam, adapters, and current depth.

prompt_templates.title: Find Deepening Opportunities
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate review of a cluster of related modules.
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze these related modules for shallow pass-through behavior. Recommend one deepening opportunity and explain the expected leverage and locality.

prompt_templates.title: Classify Dependencies
prompt_templates.prompt: Classify this module's dependencies as in-process, local-substitutable, remote owned, or true external. Recommend the right seam and adapter strategy.

prompt_templates.title: Design It Twice
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced comparison of competing interface designs.
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate three different interface designs for this refactor. Compare them by depth, locality, seam placement, dependency strategy, and testing impact.

output_examples.input: Review the checkout module interface before a payment refactor.
output_examples.output: The review identifies the current interface, notes shallow pass-through methods, and recommends a smaller payment workflow interface with injected adapters.

output_examples.input: Plan how to test a module that depends on an internal HTTP service.
output_examples.output: The plan classifies the dependency as remote but owned, proposes a port at the seam, and recommends in-memory adapters for tests.

output_examples.input: Compare alternative interfaces for a reporting workflow.
output_examples.output: The comparison explains which design offers the best leverage, where change would concentrate, and which trade-offs matter for callers.

best_practices: Provide file paths, caller examples, and dependency details before asking for interface design.
Ask for explicit depth, locality, and seam placement trade-offs in every recommendation.
Use the same terms across reviews so design discussions stay consistent.
anti_patterns: Do not introduce a seam when only one adapter exists and no variation is expected.
Do not test past the interface when behavior can be verified through the module seam.
Do not use the skill as a substitute for domain requirements or production constraints.

faq.question: What does this skill help design?
faq.answer: It helps design deep modules with small interfaces, clear seams, useful adapters, and tests focused on behavior.

faq.question: Can it review an existing codebase?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide relevant files, callers, tests, and dependencies so it can evaluate depth and seam placement.

faq.question: Does it write refactor code?
faq.answer: It can guide refactor plans, but implementation depends on the coding agent and project context.

faq.question: How is this useful with Claude Code?
faq.answer: Claude Code can use the vocabulary to discuss module interfaces and propose focused refactors.

faq.question: How is this useful with Codex?
faq.answer: Codex can apply the review language while editing code, tests, and module boundaries.

faq.question: When should I use another skill too?
faq.answer: Use another skill when the project needs domain rules, framework conventions, or product-specific architecture guidance.
